passage: I am Reena and I live upstairs from Joseph. Last Sunday his mother told him, "Give your red racing car to Kiran right now." Joseph went stiff and pulled the car to his chest. "No! It's mine!" His face looked angry, or maybe puzzled, I cannot tell. His mother crouched. "You can keep the red one special. Pick another to share." He thought, went to his box and came back with a plastic truck.

qa.q: Which toy did Joseph's mother ask him to give to Kiran?
qa.a: She asked him to give his red racing car.

qa.q: What might Joseph have been feeling when he pulled the car to his chest?
qa.a: He looked angry and maybe confused, because it was his favourite thing. Reena says it is hard to be sure what he felt.

qa.q: How did Joseph's mother's second sentence help more than her first?
qa.a: She let him keep the special car and gave him a choice to pick another toy, so sharing came from him.

qa.q: How might Reena's view of the scene differ from Joseph's experience of it?
qa.a: Reena only saw his stiff body and words, so Reena guesses. Joseph knows how much the red car mattered and how forced sharing felt.

grounding: A parent says give it now before I am ready; I am angry and confused, and a better way lets me keep one special and pick another.
